problem:
Let $f(x,y,z)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,2,-3)=-6, & \,{f}_{x}(x,y,z)=yz,\,{f}_{y}(x,y,z)=xz,\,{f}_{z}(x,y,z)=xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,-3),$ estimate the value of $f(1.01,1.95,-3.02).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,-3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,2,-3)+∇f(1,2,-3)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z+3⟩ \\  & =-6+⟨{f}_{x}(1,2,-3),{f}_{y}(1,2,-3),{f}_{z}(1,2,-3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z+3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(1,2,-3)$, ${f}_{y}(1,2,-3)$ and ${f}_{z}(1,2,-3),$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,2,-3) & =2(-3)=-6 \\ {f}_{y}(1,2,-3) & =1(-3)=-3 \\ {f}_{z}(1,2,-3) & =1(2)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y,z)≈-6+⟨-6,-3,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z+3⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(1.01,1.95,-3.02)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.01,y=1.95$ and $z=-3.02,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.01,1.95,-3.02) & ≈-6+⟨-6,-3,2⟩\cdot ⟨1.01-1,1.95-2,-3.02+3⟩ \\  & =-6+⟨-6,-3,2⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,-0.05,-0.02⟩ \\  & =-6-0.06+0.15-0.04 \\  & =-5.95\end{aligned}
$$
